guarantees.claim: When asynchronous reset is active (rst_ni low), start_valid is set to 1.
When start_i is asserted (high) and not in reset, start_valid is cleared to 0, taking priority over done_i.
When done_i is a mubi4-encoded true value (tested by mubi4_test_true_strict) and neither reset nor start_i active, start_valid is set to 1.
When none of the reset, start_i, or done_i conditions are true, start_valid retains its previous value (implicit hold).

assumptions.claim: done_i must always be driven with a legal mubi4 encoded value (either True or False); the producer must ensure both differential wires are correct.
assumptions.risk: If done_i is corrupted or not a proper mubi4 value, mubi4_test_true_strict could return false when true, leaving start_valid stuck at 0, or true spuriously, causing premature re-arming and possibly launching an unintended operation.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni must be properly synchronized and glitch-free so that the reset assertion is clean and release meets timing.
assumptions.risk: Glitches on rst_ni could cause start_valid to be spuriously set to 1, triggering a false start of a security-sensitive operation (e.g., Keccak round).

uncertain_points.claim: done_i may be asynchronous to clk_i; direct sampling in this synchronous always_ff could lead to metastability and glitches on start_valid.
uncertain_points.cond: if done_i originates from a different clock domain
uncertain_points.risk: A metastable done_i sample could cause start_valid to be set to 1 erroneously, injecting a false start into the Keccak padder, potentially corrupting the padding block or state.

uncertain_points.claim: start_i must be driven as a pulse that is deasserted before done_i to allow start_valid to return to 1; if held high it overrides done_i and prevents re-arming.
uncertain_points.risk: If start_i remains high indefinitely, start_valid will stay low, stalling the padder indefinitely even after a completed operation.
